prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Meridian Regional Air Traffic Flow Management and Airport Collaborative Decision-Making System = Regional Flow Platform (Cedarbell). Airports Meridian International, Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport keep safety authority. TOBT=Target Off Block Time: issued only if capacity/ground path allow; frozen at horizon unless exception recorded; revised only on turnaround-actor confirmation. Modes: Normal Operations (monitoring alerts); Adverse Weather Mode (Duty Manager may reduce remote stands); Capacity Reduction State (tighter escalation); both allow binding metering; Recovery Phase (remote stands absorb late arrivals); Contingency Fallback State (Contingency Operations Console). Recovery coordination in all but fallback preserves operator commercial logic. Elements: Demand Prediction Service (Marlinstone; AAR=Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module (CAM; Tactical Regulation Proposal); Slot Allocation Engine (Blueharbor; CTT=Calculated Takeoff Time; crew/rotation constraints); Departure Metering Service (Emberline; feasibility result only); North/South Runway Meters; Surface Surveillance Adapter; East/West Apron Sensors (cues; visual check where obstructed); Airport CDM Portal (Foxglove; uses shuttle count vs stand readiness; records readiness confirmation: stand, organization, time, constraint, user); Collaborative Decision Log; Tower Sequence Manager (TSM, Ironleaf; SHALL NOT advance aircraft unless remote stand release supports taxi plan); Gate Conflict Detector; Airline Interface Adapter (crew legality, no personal data); Handling Resource Planner; Alert Distribution Hub (Lantern; MUST meet latency; notifies Regional Flow Manager, Tower Supervisor, Ramp Control Lead, Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison); Ramp Movement Board (Skylark; MUST refresh within 5 s; stand states unchecked/under inspection/cleaned/blocked/ready); Common Situation Display; Audit Event Ledger; Business Rules Registry; Identity Access Service (visibility; restricts readiness confirmation to ramp/handling/airport ops roles); Sector Load Monitor (Departure Fix Load Sheet -> Regional Flow Manager); Flight Data Exchange; Performance Analytics Warehouse (anonymized legality/recovery patterns); Time Synchronization Service (time for sweeps, confirmations, releases); Arrival Regulation Console (Nightjar); Data Governance Steward; Weather Ingest Gateway (Orchard); Airspace Sector Planner; Military Airspace Liaison. Apron: stand readiness prerequisite for release; Ramp Control Lead defines sweep areas, sends Apron Sweep Completion Note, reviews hazards before pushback planning; Ground Handling Dispatcher assigns sweepers, updates Handling

Document units:
S655: Tower Supervisor does not use a stand readiness indication as clearance for aircraft movement, but the indication supports coordinated surface planning and prevents premature sequencing.
S656: Departure Metering Service suppresses release recommendations for flights whose assigned stand is not marked ready or whose access route is blocked by an unresolved apron condition.
S657: Gate Conflict Detector checks readiness status against aircraft allocation, towing activity, and adjacent stand occupancy to identify conflicts before ground movement begins.
S658: Airline Operations Coordinator may propose a revised Target Off Block Time when apron cleaning or stand restoration is expected to delay the planned turnaround.
S659: Slot Allocation Engine retains the Calculated Takeoff Time until the operational delay exceeds the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S660: Airport Duty Manager can declare a localized Capacity Reduction State when repeated apron contamination or stand closures materially reduce usable gate capacity.
S661: During Adverse Weather Mode, sweep intervals may be shortened because wind, precipitation, or deicing residue can increase the probability of foreign object debris and surface contamination.
S662: Safety-related releases are timed so that the latest sweep confirmation remains valid through passenger boarding completion, equipment removal, door closure, and pushback coordination.
S663: If the readiness validity window expires before movement begins, the stand returns to an inspection-required state and a new check is performed before release.
S664: Audit Event Ledger stores readiness changes, user acknowledgements, hazard closures, and release decisions to support post-operation review and accountability.
S665: Performance Analytics Warehouse uses aggregated readiness and contamination timing data to identify recurring debris locations, inefficient sweep patterns, and opportunities for preventive maintenance.
S666: The controlled slot swap process begins when an Aircraft Operator Representative identifies a flight that can exchange its assigned demand position without reducing declared capacity or creating an unfair priority change.
S667: The Airline Operations Coordinator enters the proposed substitution in the Airport CDM Portal with the flight identifiers, operational reason, readiness basis, and requested effective time.
S668: The Airport CDM Portal validates the submitting user through the Identity Access Service and blocks any proposal from a party without delegated operator authority.
S669: The Slot Allocation Engine evaluates the candidate swap against active Ground Delay Program constraints, Calculated Takeoff Time integrity, Target Off Block Time dependencies, and Airport Acceptance Rate commitments.
S670: The Business Rules Registry provides the governing parameters for precedence, equity, customs eligibility, minimum notification time, and prohibited trades.
